themes.title: AI Capex: Demand Versus Funding Costs
themes.status_note: Downgraded to Fading: QQQ lost 3.80% in a week; demand evidence remains, but bullish price confirmation weakened.
themes.summary: The AI spending story now faces a financing test. QQQ returned -3.80% over one week versus -1.06% for the S&P 500 (-2.74pp excess), despite remaining ahead over one month. October 14 inflation coincided with broad technology weakness. ASML still reports firm demand. Today's PPI adds inflation risk, but its US closing-price response is unavailable. Fading means price confirmation weakened; it does not establish that AI investment has collapsed.
themes.body_text:
QQQ closed at $756.20 on October 5, then fell to $747.58 on October 8 and $728.95 on October 14. The last session lost 1.97% versus the S&P 500's 1.11% decline; Nvidia, Broadcom and AMD also fell. That weakens the idea that AI demand alone can protect expensive growth shares.
The October 14 BLS release put headline inflation at 3.7% yearly. Higher financing costs are a plausible pressure on data-center investment, not a measured cause of the decline. ASML's October 14 results describe firm equipment demand, countering a demand-collapse narrative. Today's PPI release adds inflation risk but has no completed US closing-price response yet.
The marginal change is from unconditional spending optimism to scrutiny of funding and cash returns. Conviction is Med and status Fading. Watch the October 28 FOMC and November 10 CPI: sustained relative recovery plus intact customer spending would restore confirmation; funding stress and weaker orders would damage the thesis.

themes.title: Canadian Banks: Recovery Needs Proof
themes.status_note: Still Fading: ZEB recovered 1.94% in a week but lagged TSX over a month; employment weakness tests credit quality.
themes.summary: Canadian banks show a weekly repair, not a verified restart of the earnings trade. ZEB gained +1.94% in one week against +1.55% for the TSX, but its -2.24% one-month return lagged the index's -0.33%. Canada's October 9 employment report raised credit-demand questions. October 19 Bank of Canada surveys, the October 28 decision and RBC's confirmed December 3 results provide the next evidence. Status remains Fading and conviction Low.
themes.body_text:
ZEB closed at C$74.55 on September 14, C$71.49 on October 7 and C$72.88 on October 14. One-week repair of 1.94% beat the TSX's 1.55%, but the one-month decline of 2.24% lagged the index's 0.33% loss. RBC, TD and BMO each advanced over the latest week; that is breadth in a rebound, not a new earnings beat.
Statistics Canada's October 9 release reported 68,000 fewer jobs and 6.5% unemployment in September. Weaker employment could reduce loan demand or raise credit costs; that is a risk channel, not measured deterioration in bank provisions. The old earnings-momentum expectation therefore still lacks a fresh fundamental confirmation.
Status remains Fading with Low conviction. October 19 business and consumer surveys and the October 28 BoC decision test the growth backdrop. RBC confirms December 3 for its next results. Better credit outcomes and durable relative gains would strengthen the case; rising provisions or persistent monthly underperformance would weaken it.

themes.title: Energy Strength and the Supply Premium
themes.status_note: Continuing: XLE gained 6.74% in a week; supply risk persists, but weaker demand and low volume temper conviction.
themes.summary: Energy remains the strongest measured theme: XLE returned +6.74% in one week versus -1.06% for the S&P 500, an +7.80pp spread. October 14's IEA report describes fragile supply recovery alongside falling demand. Exxon, Chevron and ConocoPhillips participated in the weekly rise. The signal is continuing relative strength, not a claim that energy equities track crude one-for-one. Latest XLE volume was below its preceding 20-session average.
themes.body_text:
XLE moved from $64.53 on September 14 to $65.24 on October 8 and $67.63 on October 14. Its one-week gain of 6.74% beat the S&P 500's 1.06% loss. Exxon, Chevron and ConocoPhillips all rose over that week. WTI's October 14 daily bar was $95.09, but its one-month return was negative: energy stocks and crude are different exposures.
The October 14 IEA report describes renewed regional supply risks, fragile export recovery and continued market deficits, while also cutting demand expectations. This supports a conditional supply-premium explanation; demand destruction is the competing case, not a detail to hide.
Status stays Continuing with Med conviction. Volume confirmation is false at 0.75x the preceding 20-session average, so price breadth alone does not justify High conviction. The next scheduled EIA report on October 21 can test inventories. Repeated stock builds and normalizing supply would undermine the premium; further tightness would support it.

themes.title: High Yields: The Bond Selloff Pauses
themes.status_note: Downgraded to Fading: the 10Y eased to 5.19% and TLT gained 2.26% over a week despite hot CPI.
themes.summary: The earlier rising-yield thesis has lost near-term price confirmation. TLT returned +2.26% in one week versus -1.06% for the S&P 500; the 10-year yield eased from 5.311% on October 5 to 5.190% on October 14. Inflation is still a risk, and today's PPI reinforces it, but hot data has not yet produced another sustained bond selloff. Status is Fading, with the next FOMC decision the main test.
themes.body_text:
The October 5 observation was a 5.311% 10-year yield and a $77.11 TLT close. By October 8 TLT was $77.87; on October 14 it reached $78.89 as the yield eased to 5.190%. TLT gained 2.26% over one week, although its one-month return remained negative.
October 14 CPI raised the inflation concern, yet bonds rallied that session. Today's October 15 PPI release adds a 1.3% monthly and 6.3% yearly increase in final-demand producer prices; no completed US closing reaction is available for it yet. The divergence prevents a claim that higher inflation mechanically means higher long yields every day.
The prior expectation was a persistent long-bond selloff; the marginal evidence is a rebound. Status moves to Fading, conviction Med. A lower TLT price would confirm the higher-yield direction; its returns are shown without sign inversion. The October 28 FOMC and November 10 CPI are the tests. A sustained yield break below 5% would further weaken the thesis; renewed highs would revive it.
